name: TinyZKP Evaluation Kit
summary: Business-case and technical evaluation kit for deciding whether TinyZKP proof receipts belong in one agent, API, audit, or Compute workflow.

evaluation_positioning.primary_question: Does a portable proof receipt change the trust boundary for one consequential state transition?
best_for: AI agent actions with customer, money, record, permission, or workflow consequences
Backend API mutations where a customer or downstream service benefits from verification
Audit, reserve, liability, inventory, or reconciliation checkpoints
Long supported state-transition traces where high-RAM prover operations are the alternative

evaluation_steps.action: Choose one workflow and name the verifier who should trust the receipt.
evaluation_steps.output: Workflow owner, verifier, and business decision are explicit.

evaluation_steps.action: Check whether the statement fits the live template or needs pilot review.
evaluation_steps.output: Template fit, design-review need, and data boundary are known.

evaluation_steps.action: Generate or inspect a receipt and verify it through the public verifier or API.
evaluation_steps.output: Receipt artifact and verifier result exist.

evaluation_steps.action: Estimate monthly volume, trace-size band, plan fit, and Compute applicability.
evaluation_steps.output: Expected cost, cap behavior, and commercial path are documented.

evaluation_steps.action: Choose start free, upgrade self-serve, run pilot, request enterprise, or defer.
evaluation_steps.output: Go/no-go decision and next owner are clear.

stakeholders.cares_about: Whether a receipt changes trust, sales, support, audit, or customer experience.
How to generate, attach, poll, and verify receipts without rebuilding the workflow.
What data enters TinyZKP, what is public, and what is not claimed by default.
Whether receipt cost is lower than replay, audit exports, support work, or prover operations.
Vendor review, support path, release policy, pricing, privacy, and security packet completeness.

decision_criteria.pass_signal: A recipient needs to verify the encoded state transition without trusting the source system.
The receipt URL, proof object, badge, or agent envelope appears where the verifier will see it.
The live template covers the workflow or the custom statement is narrow enough for pilot review.
decision_criteria.route: Use self-serve if live; use pilot if custom.

decision_criteria.pass_signal: Transparent parameters contain only public or approved values.
decision_criteria.route: Proceed; otherwise pause for privacy review.

decision_criteria.pass_signal: The receipt replaces replay, manual evidence, support work, audit exports, or prover operations.
decision_criteria.route: Proceed with calculator and buying path.

roi_drivers.economic_reason: Reviewers can verify the encoded transition without accessing or replaying the producer system.
Agent outputs can carry machine-checkable proof for approvals, payments, records, and checkpoints.
roi_drivers.evidence: Agent receipt envelope or receipt URL attached to output.

roi_drivers.economic_reason: Long traces can move away from high-RAM workers, custom queues, segmentation, and on-call ownership.
Public trust, pricing, schemas, OpenAPI, changelog, and evaluation metadata reduce bespoke review cycles.

go: A real verifier benefits from checking the receipt.
The workflow can be encoded as a supported state transition or scoped pilot.
Transparent public parameters are acceptable for the first rollout.
Expected cost is clearer than replay, manual evidence, or prover operations.

evidence_to_collect: Receipt URL, proof object, or agent receipt envelope from the target workflow.
Fit Finder summary showing workflow, verifier, receipt placement, data boundary, expected volume, and recommended route.
Verifier result from public verifier, API verifier, SDK, CLI, or compatible WASM path.
Plain-language statement boundary describing what the receipt proves and does not prove.
Monthly volume, trace-size band, plan recommendation, spend cap, or Compute estimate.
Security and procurement packet links for data handling, proof scope, status, schemas, pricing, and release policy.
Rollout decision: start free, upgrade self-serve, run pilot, request reserved capacity, or defer.

recommended_paths.trigger: Internal demo or early agent workflow
Custom statement, procurement, support commitments, or reserved capacity
Agent platform, IDE, workflow engine, or marketplace rollout
recommended_paths.path: $5,000 Production Pilot then sales-assisted platform rollout from $499/month minimum plus usage
